src%2Fvfs%2Fbase.py%23grant%20revoke%20posture::src%2Fvfs%2Fstorage%2Fbackends%2Fdatabase%2Frights.py%23grant%20and%20posture%20gate::src%2Fvfs%2Fstorage::ATTACK-CLASSES.md%23Access%20control :: this unit, the membership unit and the grants-listing unit each excluded 'Deletion, revocation, and lifecycle' by pointing at a peer, and unit 30 owns that class only for posture labels. I checked revocation freshness against source myself. resolve_authority (rights.py:351-357) revalidates every cached compile on each call against principal_revision stamps it reads from the database, so the check also works across processes. grant_rows, revoke_rows, add_member_rows, remove_member_rows and set_posture each bump the revision and stamp the principal they affect (rights.py:918, 961, 1032, 1080, 1111). Closure ids are recorded at compile time, and a nested-group change stamps the member group, which is in every affected caller's ids. A compile whose opening and closing revisions disagree is answered but not cached (rights.py:376-377). Grant rows are path-anchored and are not purged by sweep (trash.py:567-591) or moved by move. Spec 058 sections 0 and 6 decide this: coverage is by prefix, and a move is a permission event. So a residual grant behaves like any directory grant, not like a new boundary failure. No new unit is needed.
